prompt.brief: Design a generative image and video platform that accepts prompts and source media, schedules GPU inference and fine-tuning jobs, filters unsafe content, and serves durable results at scale.
successSignals: Separate immutable prompts, input assets, model and adapter versions, job state, moderation decisions, and generated assets.
Use queue-backed GPU scheduling, batching where safe, quotas, cancellation, and per-tenant fairness for expensive workloads.
Apply prompt and output safety checks, provenance and watermark policy, copyright controls, and explicit content states.
Explain retries, deterministic seeds, model cache warming, partial video failure, privacy, deletion, and cost controls.

functional: Create image or video jobs, upload inputs, select an approved model or adapter, generate variants, and retrieve results.
Expose queued, running, moderation, completed, failed, and canceled states with progress, seed, model, and cost metadata.
Support fine-tuning datasets, access controls, abuse reports, asset deletion, usage quotas, and signed result URLs.
nonFunctional: Target p95 image generation below 10 seconds for the standard preset; video and fine-tuning are asynchronous jobs.
Scale GPU queues by model, resolution, frame count, and tenant while preventing one large job from starving short jobs.
Make job submission, asset writes, moderation, and billing idempotent; never charge twice for one attempt.
Keep completed assets available and queue work when a model host or GPU pool is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Support 100,000 generations per hour, 10,000 concurrent jobs, and multiple image and video model families.
Partition queues by model and tenant; isolate high-resolution video and fine-tuning workloads.
Retain encrypted inputs, prompts, model manifests, moderation outcomes, and outputs under tenant retention policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Generative image commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Generative image writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Generative image version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Generative image by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Generative image work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Generative image projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Generative image projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Generative image records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Generative image latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines job submission, GPU scheduling, safety, artifact delivery, scale, latency, durability, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys cover tenants, jobs, model versions, input manifests, moderation decisions, artifacts, and lifecycle transitions.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Generative image consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
